question: What's the difference between CSC-221 and CSC-241?
ground_truth: Both are 2-credit CSC courses with CSC-121 as the prerequisite, but the topic differs: CSC-221 (Topics in Programming) is an intensive course where students study a new programming language or paradigm — the topic varies and the course can be repeated. CSC-241 (Mobile Apps) is specifically about developing applications for mobile platforms (iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad).
notes: Comparative reasoning across two rows. Tests whether the system contrasts rather than just listing both descriptions.

question: Are there any courses that count for both the HB (Empirical Study of Human Behavior) GER and the WC (World Cultures) GER?
ground_truth: Yes — there are 12 unique courses listed under combined 'HB and WC' GER labels in hb.csv. The labels appear with several inconsistent string variants: 7 rows under 'HB (Empirical Study of Human Behavior) and WC (World Cultures)', 2 under 'HB ... and WC ... and IEJ ...' (triple GER), 1 under 'HB (Empirical Studies of Human Behavior)' (note plural), 1 with reversed order 'WC ... and HB ...', and 1 with lowercase 'human behavior'. The string inconsistencies make this a stress test for exact-match retrieval.
notes: Original GT says '14 courses' but my actual count of unique codes intersecting hb.csv ∩ wc.csv is 12. The original may be counting label-variant rows (some courses have entries under multiple variant labels) rather than unique course codes. Either reading is defensible — flag this ambiguity for the question author.

question: Who teaches MHC courses, and how many are there?
ground_truth: There is exactly 1 MHC course in the catalog: MHC-503 (Individualized Internship). Instructor information is NOT in the source data — the catalog CSVs do not have an instructor column, so the question's 'who teaches' part cannot be answered from this corpus. A correct answer must say so explicitly rather than hallucinate an instructor name.
notes: Tests honest refusal. The CSV columns are coid/code/title/ger/prerequisites/description/credits — no instructor field. A model that invents a name fails the test.

question: Are there any courses listed under the major prefix NLY?
ground_truth: No. There is no nly.csv file under 'courses by majors/' (the prefix doesn't exist as a major), but nly.csv DOES exist under 'courses by GER/' as the 'Natural World Lab' GER list, with 7 courses. So the answer depends on interpretation: as a major prefix → no NLY major exists; as a GER → 7 courses fulfill the NLY GER.
notes: Original GT says 'nly.csv exists but contains no course records (header row only, 0 courses)' — this is INCORRECT. The actual nly.csv (in courses by GER/) has 7 rows. The 'major prefix NLY' framing is the wrong frame: NLY is a GER, not a major. Question author may have been thinking of a different version of the corpus. Recommend question rewrite to disambiguate 'major prefix' vs 'GER prefix'.

question: What is CSC-475 and what are its prerequisites?
ground_truth: CSC-475 is 'Seminar in Computer Science', 4 credits. It fulfills the WR (Writing-Research Intensive) GER. Students prepare papers on topics from CS research journals and give oral presentations; enrollment is limited to juniors and seniors. The prerequisites are 'any first year writing seminar, CSC-122, and one CSC course numbered 300 or greater' — but these prerequisites are written into the start of the description text rather than the dedicated prerequisites column, which is empty for this course.
notes: Data quality probe. Tests inferential robustness: a system relying only on the prereq column would say 'no prerequisites'; reading description recovers the truth.

question: How many credits is CSC-372?
ground_truth: 4 credits. The credits column is empty for CSC-372 in the CSV, but the description text ends with '...real world problem domain. 4'. Other CSC 300/400-level courses with similar intensity are 4 credits, and the trailing '4' in the description is the credit value. This is the same data-quality issue as a few other rows where the credit value got entered at the tail of the description rather than in the credits column.
notes: Same class of data-quality issue as q14. The dedicated credits column is empty; the value is at the tail of description.

question: I want to take an introductory course on artificial intelligence. What does Furman offer?
ground_truth: Furman offers several CSC courses related to AI/ML at different levels: CSC-272 (Introduction to Data Mining), CSC-343 (Artificial Intelligence), and CSC-372 (Machine Learning with Big Data). For a true introduction, CSC-343 is the AI-titled course; CSC-272 is the most directly introductory in spirit (data mining/ML foundations). CSC-105 (Intro to CS) mentions AI as one possible theme but isn't AI-specific.
notes: Subjective question — multiple courses are reasonable answers. Tests whether the system surfaces multiple options + their differences, or picks one without explanation.

question: I want to take CSC-372 next semester. What sequence of CSC and MTH courses do I need to complete first?
ground_truth: To take CSC-372 (Machine Learning with Big Data) — prereqs are (CSC-122 AND CSC-272) AND (MTH-120 OR MTH-150). Working backwards: CSC-122 itself requires CSC-121 (Intro to Computer Programming). CSC-272 requires CSC-122 (so same chain). MTH-120 (Calculus I) and MTH-150 (Calculus with Theory) are independent prereqs. Minimal sequence: CSC-121 → CSC-122 → CSC-272 → CSC-372, alongside MTH-120 OR MTH-150 anywhere before CSC-372.
notes: Multi-hop prerequisite resolution. Tests whether the system traces the dependency graph rather than just listing the immediate prereqs of CSC-372.

question: What writing-intensive courses (GER: WR) does the Computer Science department offer?
ground_truth: Two CSC courses fulfill the WR (Writing-Research Intensive) GER: CSC-475 (Seminar in Computer Science) and CSC-502 (Research). Both are upper-division.

question: What are the requirements for a Senior Capstone in the Sustainability Studies major?
ground_truth: The Sustainability Studies major has TWO capstone courses, not one: SUS-474 (Senior Capstone) — synthesis course integrating research experience across EES and SUS majors with focus on writing, collaboration, and communication; and SUS-473 (Sustainability Science Practicum) — applied solution-based research conducted at the local level in partnership with local organizations. SUS-473 has a prerequisite of 'any first year writing seminar'; SUS-474's prerequisites column is empty.
notes: Two courses match 'capstone' criteria; the question implies one but there are two. A complete answer surfaces both and explains the difference.

question: I'm interested in cryptography. What courses can I take?
ground_truth: Two courses are most relevant: CSC-362 (Information Security) — covers cryptographic primitives in the context of information security; and MTH-320 (Number Theory) — number theory is the mathematical foundation of modern cryptography. There is no course titled 'Cryptography' specifically. CSC-362 is the most direct hit.
notes: Topic search across descriptions. Tests whether the system surfaces both the applied (CSC-362) and foundational (MTH-320) angles.
